title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Bitbucket Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Bitbucket Cloud SaaS; workspace/project access tokens and IP allowlisting need Premium, org-level audit log needs Atlassian Guard; API tokens are Atlassian-account tokens shared with Jira/Confluence.

controls.name: Pipelines oidc option
controls.what: Set oidc to false in bitbucket-pipelines.yml to stop issuing the step OIDC token.

controls_unknown: Whether the workspace IP allowlist is enforced on REST API calls (docs only mention viewing content and Git clone/push/pull).
Whether API tokens or OAuth tokens are checked against IdP SSO or conditional access at use time.
Whether the workspace audit log records access token creation, rotation or revocation (no such events listed).
Lifetime of the Pipelines OIDC token.
OAuth access token lifetime: developer docs say 1 hour, support docs say 2 hours.
Any admin approval workflow for users authorizing third-party OAuth consumers.

authentication.summary: A Pipelines step with oidc enabled gets a signed OIDC token in BITBUCKET_STEP_OIDC_TOKEN, which it exchanges with AWS, GCP or Vault for cloud credentials.

federation.details: Outbound federation; trust and claim conditions are enforced by the resource server.

ip_restriction.boundary: Restriction to Bitbucket Pipelines IP ranges is configured in the resource server's trust policy (AWS, GCP, Vault); Bitbucket itself has no setting.

administration.summary: Control lives in the resource server trust policy (audience, repository/deployment claims). Anyone who can edit bitbucket-pipelines.yml can request the token.

offboard.details: Issued by Bitbucket Pipelines to a pipeline step for use at a resource server, not tied to a user's account.

disable.cli: bitbucket-pipelines.yml: set oidc: false on the step

network.ui: AWS IAM > role > Trust relationships: add a source-IP condition listing Bitbucket Pipelines IP ranges

log_sources.name: Cloud provider logs (e.g. AWS CloudTrail AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity)
log_sources.notes: Use is visible at the resource server, not Bitbucket.

credential_id_fields.notes: Claims shown on the Pipelines OpenID Connect settings page.

anomaly_cues: Role assumption from a branch or environment not in the trust policy
Pipeline YAML changes that add oidc: true

containment.steps: Tighten or delete the trust policy at the resource server; set oidc false.
containment.notes: Already-issued cloud credentials last until their own expiry.

unknown: Holder calls the cloud provider, not Bitbucket

evidence.title: Integrate Pipelines with resource servers using OIDC
Deploy on AWS using Bitbucket Pipelines OpenID Connect
